newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 28.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 28.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing,
Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

NEW YORK - Golf sensation Tiger Woods has signed a contract with Rolex Watch U.S.A. Inc. to endorse a new line of luxury watches being introduced by its Tudor brand, Rolex says. Rolex is the latest prestige name to enter into an endorsement agreement with Woods, the youngest ever Master's champion.
CANBERRA - Australian Finance Minister John Fahey says Burson-Marsteller will manage public relations issues surrounding the partial sale of telecoms carrier Telstra Corp.
WASHINGTON - Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt is set to announce his plans to leave the agency, according to sources close to the FCC.

SAN FRANCISCO - Marketing consultancy Bass Yager and Lloyd Northover Citigate, a division of the Citigate public relations and advertising group, say they have formed a strategic marketing and creative partnership.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
LONDON - The Internet offers vast commercial opportunities, but Websites must be well designed, promoted and marketed if they are to succeed, Internet experts say.

BRUSSELS - A group of EU states, concerned that the European Commission may try to clamp down on subsidies to public television broadcasters, is proposing to exclude the sector altogether from competition rules. Belgium, Sweden, Portugal, Germany, Italy and Greece are discussing the matter and France, Austria, Finland, Ireland and Luxembourg also express concern.

LONDON - Television continues to be a strong growth market in Central and Eastern Europe, but an increasing push for locally-produced programmes is taking hold as markets mature. Local viewers and governments are getting fed up with too much imported American programming.

BERLIN - German private television station Sat1 signs up licensing agency BMC of Munich to market its booming merchandise sales. BMC will take on marketing activities for Sat1 licensed products which are not advertised on-air,
effective June 1, the station says.

NEW YORK - PrimeStar Partners has reached a tentative agreement for News Corp Ltd to join the satellite-dish TV service as a partner, according to sources close to the matter. The two sides are continuing their discussions, which are described as fragile and ongoing.

MOUNTAIN VIEW, California - Netscape Communications Corp. and other firms propose a global standard aimed at protecting security of Internet users. In a statement, Netscape, Firefly Network Inc, Verisign Inc. and more than 60 leading companies and organizations announce support for the Open Profiling Standard, that will enable people to exchange personal profile information over the Internet.
BONN - Germany's federal post minister Wolfgang Boetsch will decide on a policy on digital technology in the television arena in the coming weeks, according to all-news network n-tv.

HANOI - Vietnam announces rules preventing a range of state bodies from releasing information on the Internet and requiring diplomats and foreign organisations to seek approval to transmit information online.
HELSINKI - Finnish telecoms group Nokia Oy says it will deliver 50,000 digital TV decoders to Spanish broadcasting company Via Digital. It does not give the value of the deal.

NUREMBERG - Media market research company GfK says it is considering a public share listing in 1999. It says it plans to expand consolidated group turnover to over 650 million marks ($381.7 million) before 2000.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

LONDON - The collapse of communism in Central and Eastern Europe sent Western-based multinationals stampeding into the region, but experts say many companies have since been burned by Europe's emerging consumer markets.

LONDON - Some U.K. petrol stations selling the Esso brand claim the U.S.-based oil giant is demanding nearly 50 million pounds ($81.6 million) in charges tied to the defunct Tiger Token promotional scheme that ended in 1996 after a 10-year run. The Esso Licensed Retailers Association (ELRA), representing some 600 stations, say the cost to each licensee for participating in the program was increased at the same time the company was launching its Pricewatch campaign early last year.

BONN - Retail giant Metro AG, born out of a merger with three store chains last year, impresses investors by hitting 1996 profit targets and said it would seek to grow its business internationally. Metro says its group income on ordinary activities was 1.062 billion marks while debut net profits came in at 717 million marks.

ATLANTA - Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc., the largest of the Coke bottlers, is embarking on a bold new plan to consolidate the United States and Canada into a single market for Coke-brand soft drinks, analysts say.

PARIS - Carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen has lowered its estimate for the French car market to 1.85 million sales this year, a 13 percent fall from 2.13 million in 1996. "Since October, we continue to have monthly order declines of between 20 and 22 percent," PSA chairman Jacques Calvet says

STUTTGART - Daimler-Benz AG Chairman Juergen Schrempp says he expects 1997 car sales to climb to over 700,000 from 645,000 in 1996. He says European truck orders were up 45 percent in the first four months of 1997.

BRUSSELS - The European Union and Mexico sign a mutual recognition accord for their leading spirit drinks, which is expected to boost bilateral trade in whisky, cognac, tequila and other spirits. The deal means Mexico cannot market home grown versions of Scotch whisky and French champagne under the names of their European rivals. Similarly, European drinks manufacturers are forbidden from producing the traditional
Mexican spirits tequila and mezcal.
STUTTGART - Daimler-Benz AG Chairman Juergen Schrempp says he expects 1997 car sales to climb to over 700,000 from 645,000 in 1996.

TOKYO - Sega Enterprises Ltd says it accepts computer gaming company Bandai Co Ltd's request to cancel a planned merger. However, Sega says it has accepted Bandai's alternative offer of a business tie-up. Bandai's business has recently been boosted by the popularity of its "Tamagotchi" electronic pet toy.

OTTAWA - Foreigners from the United States and overseas made a record 17.3 million overnight trips to Canada in 1996, injecting an unprecedented C$9.6 billion ($6.9 billion) into the Canadian economy, researchers Statistics Canada says.

SACRAMENTO, California - Body piercing is increasingly popular in California but teens wanting to have their ears, lips or tongues pierced will have to show they have parents permission under new legislation.
LOS ANGELES - Dinosaurs are back. Steven Spielberg's new dinosaur movie "The Lost World" the sequel to Jurassic Park has trampled box office records.

JERUSALEM - Chewing gum fans in Palestine may get more than they bargained for according to a Palestinian Authority official who accuses Israel of sending chewing gum spiked with aphrodisiacs and sterility-inducing drugs into the West Bank and Gaza Strip. An Israeli government spokesman calls the charges
"outrageous."
